identity_snapshot.short_description: A civilization of walled refuges, paladin orders, and Beacon-light, built on the conviction that the strong must shelter the weak and that protection is only just when it is accountable.
identity_snapshot.civilization_type: Civic-religious federation of warded refuge-cities governed by covenant, oath, and public accountability.
identity_snapshot.core_belief: Protection is sacred only when it shelters the vulnerable and answers to the people it claims to guard.
identity_snapshot.domain_stone_or_source: The Concord Beacon — the principal Beacon of a network anchored to the Sanctuary Stone fragment.
identity_snapshot.magic_style: Beacon-warding and covenant-oath magic: shelter, light, healing, and binding vows of protection.
identity_snapshot.main_magic_cost: Oath burden and public trust — a ward holds only as long as the covenant behind it is honored.
identity_snapshot.political_center: The Concord Hall beneath the great Beacon at Lumenhaven.
identity_snapshot.military_identity: Defensive guardians: hold the walls, shield civilians, never strike the helpless.
identity_snapshot.economic_base: Refuge logistics, warded trade, healing-houses, manufacture, and pilgrimage to the Beacons.
identity_snapshot.biggest_internal_conflict: Whether safety justifies closing the gates and purging the suspect (Purity Inquisition) or whether protection means open shelter and due process (Refugee Covenant).
identity_snapshot.biggest_external_threat: Abyss infiltration — Ash Ledger soul-debt contracts and collaborator magistrates hollowing Sanctuary from within.
identity_snapshot.keeper_exploit: The Keeper turns Sanctuary's protection into paranoid control, so it cages the very people it swore to shelter and shatters its own unity with suspicion.
identity_snapshot.void_lie: You cannot protect them if you cannot watch them; safety is worth a little surrender.

canon_facts: Sanctuary is lit and warded by the Beacon network, anchored to a fragment of the fractured pure Nexus Stone.
Paladin orders swear public covenant-oaths to shelter the vulnerable; an oath broken in secret weakens the Beacons.
Sanctuary governs by accountable covenant; magistrates answer to public review, at least in principle.
Refuge-cities take in those fleeing the Abyss frontier, straining resources and stoking the gate-closure debate.
The Purity Inquisition pushes containment and purges; the Refugee Covenant defends open shelter and due process.
Abyss Ash Ledger agents and collaborator magistrates are Sanctuary's gravest hidden threat.
cannot_contradict: Sanctuary magic and authority must always rest on accountable covenant; protection without accountability is its corruption.
Sanctuary corruption must distort protection into control and unity into purity-paranoia, never become generic darkness.
Sanctuary internal politics must respect the Concord / Inquisition / Covenant / paladin fracture.
Beacon wards weaken when covenant-oaths are broken or when the sheltered are betrayed.

metaphysical_role.principle_embodied: Protection and unity — the binding of the strong to shelter the weak, made real through kept covenant.
metaphysical_role.nexus_stone_aspect: The Stone's capacity to shelter and gather — light that holds many souls safe within one warded whole.
metaphysical_role.soul_flow_shaped: Sanctuary lets the sheltered dead rest under the Beacon's light, accounted-for and named, rather than lost or harvested.
metaphysical_role.natural_magic: Beacon-warding and covenant-oath: protective light, healing, and vows that bind the powerful to the vulnerable.
metaphysical_role.when_extreme: Protection hardens into a cage; unity calcifies into enforced sameness and the hunt for the impure.
metaphysical_role.keeper_exploits_extremity: The Keeper feeds the fear that safety requires control, so Sanctuary surveils, purges, and excludes until its covenant — and its Beacons — fail.

domain_stone.origin: Kindled atop a fragment of the fractured pure Nexus Stone by the first Covenant, lit ever since by kept oaths of protection across the Beacon network.
domain_stone.public_knowledge: The Beacons keep the wards lit and the refuges safe; they shine as long as the Covenant is honored.
domain_stone.hidden_truth: Secret oath-breaking by collaborator magistrates and the quiet surrender of registries to Ash Ledger agents are dimming the network from within; some border Beacons gutter.
failure_symptoms: Names vanishing from the rolls of the protected
healing_methods: Re-naming the disappeared into the light
domain_stone.keeper_attack_vector: Tempt magistrates into secret oath-breaking so the Beacon network dims unseen.
domain_stone.void_attack_vector: Offer perfect security through surveillance and registries that quietly become harvest lists.

soul_flow.healthy_soul_flow_description: The sheltered dead rest accounted-for under the Beacon's light, their names kept on the rolls and mourned in the open.
soul_flow.damaged_soul_flow_description: The disappeared and the unaccounted are erased from the rolls and bound by Ash Ledger contracts, their names harvested into soul-debt.
forbidden_soul_processes: Erasing a name from the protected rolls
Secret detention that hides a soul from the light
common_soul_wounds: The unmourned hidden by falsified records
soul_flow.keeper_disruption_strategy: Turn protective registries into instruments of disappearance and debt.
soul_flow.void_disruption_strategy: Whisper that watching everyone is the only way to keep anyone safe.

true_virtues.name: Protection
true_virtues.healthy_definition: The duty of the strong to shelter the vulnerable, bounded by accountability to those sheltered.
true_virtues.cultural_expression: Every household keeps a refuge-light for any traveler in need.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: A paladin shields a stranger first and asks their name after.
true_virtues.political_expression: Magistrates are judged by whom they keep safe, not whom they exclude.
true_virtues.magical_expression: Beacon-wards strengthen when the sheltered are genuinely protected.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Refuge logistics are funded as a shared covenant, not charity.
true_virtues.military_expression: The walls are held for the weak behind them; the helpless are never struck.
true_virtues.common_saying: A wall that does not shelter is only a cage.

true_virtues.name: Accountability
true_virtues.healthy_definition: The principle that power must answer, in the open, to those it claims to serve.
true_virtues.cultural_expression: Wrongs are aired at public review beneath the Beacon, not buried.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: An official confesses a failure rather than hide it.
true_virtues.political_expression: Authority is legitimate only while it submits to review.
true_virtues.magical_expression: Covenant-oaths are sworn publicly so they can be publicly kept.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Refuge ledgers are open to inspection.
true_virtues.military_expression: Paladins answer for every use of force.
true_virtues.common_saying: Light hides nothing, and neither should we.

true_virtues.name: Unity
true_virtues.healthy_definition: Solidarity that includes the stranger and the suspect, bound by shared shelter rather than sameness.
true_virtues.heroic_expression: A citizen defends a distrusted outsider's right to due process.
true_virtues.political_expression: The Concord seeks consensus that protects minorities, not majorities alone.
true_virtues.magical_expression: The Beacon network shines brightest when the refuges act as one.
true_virtues.economic_expression: Burdens of intake are shared across cities, not dumped on the border.
true_virtues.military_expression: Cities reinforce one another's walls without price.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: Protection that controls, surveils, and detains the very people it claims to shelter.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: A genuine infiltration scare makes surveillance and detention feel like simple prudence.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Fear, the comfort of 'nothing to hide,' and officials who gain power by promising safety.
who_benefits: Ash Ledger agents (who love a registry)
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Sanctuary's protective machinery becomes a tool of disappearance and division.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: You cannot protect them if you cannot watch them.
visible_symptoms: Wards turned inward on the sheltered
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: Sanctuary becomes the prison it was built to prevent, and its Beacons dim.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: The belief that unity requires sameness, and that safety means purging the impure and the outsider.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: A real collaborator is found, and the hunt does not stop at the guilty.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Sermons of contamination, witch-hunt momentum, and the thrill of certainty.
who_benefits: Abyss, which thrives on Sanctuary's broken unity
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Fractures Sanctuary's unity and recruits its enemies from its own outcasts.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: The impure cannot be trusted; mercy toward them is a door left open.
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: Sanctuary devours its own and drives the excluded into the Abyss's arms.

corrupted_virtues.corrupted_definition: The hollowing of accountability — review becomes theater while the real records are hidden or falsified.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_begins: An official falsifies a record once, for a good reason, and learns the rolls can lie.
corrupted_virtues.how_it_spreads: Convenience, cover-ups protecting allies, and Ash Ledger infiltration of the archives.
who_suffers: The public who trust the rolls
corrupted_virtues.keeper_benefit: Lets soul-debt and disappearance spread under a mask of order.
corrupted_virtues.void_lie: Some truths only frighten people; better the rolls stay clean.
visible_symptoms: Reviews that never reach real findings
Names quietly struck from the rolls
corrupted_virtues.late_stage_consequence: The Beacons dim as their covenant rots behind a façade of order.

keeper_exploit_pattern.corruption_strategy: Inflate an infiltration fear until protection becomes surveillance and unity becomes purge, so Sanctuary cages the sheltered and burns its own trust.
preferred_crisis_conditions: A refugee surge straining a border city
A public scandal involving forbidden magic
keeper_exploit_pattern.domain_stone_damage_type: Beacon dimming as covenant-oaths are broken and the sheltered are betrayed.
keeper_exploit_pattern.common_lie: Safety is worth a little surrender; the innocent have nothing to fear.
keeper_exploit_pattern.long_term_goal: Convert Sanctuary's protective network into an engine of surveillance and disappearance, snuffing the Beacons that hold the prison's light.

void_temptation_pattern.temptation_phrase: You cannot protect them if you cannot watch them.
void_temptation_pattern.immediate_benefit: Total surveillance and pre-emptive detention catch real threats fast and make the city feel safe.
void_temptation_pattern.hidden_cost: The registries become harvest lists; the disappeared are bound to soul-debt and the Beacon dims.
void_temptation_pattern.identity_damage: Protectors begin to see the sheltered as suspects, losing the covenant that defined them.
void_temptation_pattern.soul_flow_damage: Names slip from the protected rolls into Ash Ledger contracts.
void_temptation_pattern.reality_damage: Warded districts grow gray and joyless; the Beacon's light cools where trust dies.
visible_stage_3_symptoms: The protected indistinguishable from the imprisoned

magic_systems.source: The Beacon network and the Sanctuary Stone fragment, sustained by kept covenant.
political_use: Lighting a city into the Concord
magic_systems.keeper_corruption_vector: Turn the protective ward into a watching eye.
magic_systems.void_enhancement_vector: Offer surveillance-wards that see everything and dim the Beacon.

magic_systems.source: Public vows of protection bound into the Beacon's light.
battlefield_use: Binding a sworn protector to the defended
abuse_modes: Oaths of loyalty that override shelter
magic_systems.keeper_corruption_vector: Replace oaths of shelter with oaths of obedience.
magic_systems.void_enhancement_vector: Offer power for a secretly broken oath, dimming the Beacon a little each time.

magic_costs.description: Covenant magic binds the swearer under public vows of protection that carry real weight.
magic_costs.moderate_effect: The vow felt as constant obligation; rest disturbed when it is strained.
magic_costs.severe_effect: A broken protective oath becomes a hollowing wound and dims the nearest Beacon.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Honoring the vow, or publicly confessing and making amends.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: Oath corrosion the Keeper exploits into Beacon failure.

magic_costs.description: Wards and covenants draw on public trust; coercion and secrecy drain it.
magic_costs.moderate_effect: Districts withhold cooperation; wards weaken over them.
magic_costs.severe_effect: Collapse of civic trust; the ward fails and the city fractures.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Open accountability, restored shelter, and kept promises.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: A trust-broken city the Inquisition can radicalize.

magic_costs.description: Turning wards inward or lighting only the favored strains the Beacon network.
magic_costs.minor_effect: A dimming flicker in the local Beacon.
magic_costs.moderate_effect: Wards fail over neglected districts; a border Beacon gutters.
magic_costs.severe_effect: A Beacon goes dark; the disappeared multiply beneath it.
magic_costs.recovery_method: Re-extend shelter to all, restore broken covenants, re-light the Beacon.
magic_costs.permanent_risk: Network-wide Beacon failure if strain spreads.

government.government_type: Civic-religious federation of refuge-cities governed by accountable covenant and public review.
government.ruling_body: The Sanctuary Concord, seated at Lumenhaven beneath the great Beacon.
government.religious_authority: The Lumen Wardens, keepers of the Beacons and covenant doctrine.
government.military_authority: The Aegis paladin orders and the city Watch.

government.magical_authority: Lumen Wardens certify wards; the oath-courts govern covenants.
government.succession_or_selection_method: Magistrates are elected or covenant-appointed and bound to public review; office is forfeit for a broken oath.
government.legitimacy_source: Kept covenant, accountable review, and the steady light of the Beacons.
known_cracks_in_legitimacy: The Buried Ledger hiding collaborator magistrates
Border cities feeling sacrificed by the interior

burdens: Answerable for every use of force
Caught between shelter and Inquisition orders
class_structure.military_obligation: Hold the walls and shield civilians.
class_structure.economic_role: Stipended by the Concord; forbidden private war-profit.

Blamed when the Concord's failures reach the walls

A name on the protected rolls

Disappeared if the Buried Ledger spreads

downward_mobility_risks: Signing an Ash Ledger survival contract

economy.wartime_economy_behavior: Diverts everything to refuge intake and wall-holding; scarcity fuels the gate-closure debate and black-market debt.
famine_or_shortage_risks: Border supply lines cut by the Abyss
Sap or arms embargo from neighbors
exploitative_practices: Selling places on the protected rolls
economy.keeper_attack_vector: Engineer a refuge-food crisis so Sanctuary closes its gates and turns to surveillance and debt.

military_doctrine.strategic_identity: Defend, shelter, and endure; never strike the helpless, never abandon the sheltered.
military_doctrine.defensive_strategy: Layered wards and shield-walls protecting evacuation; trade ground to save lives.
military_doctrine.offensive_strategy: Rare and surgical: root out infiltration, never raze.
military_doctrine.logistics_strategy: Refuge networks and Beacon signals; vulnerable to food shortage and archive sabotage.
military_doctrine.intelligence_strategy: Paladin reports and warden sight; dangerously vulnerable to Ash Ledger infiltration and the Buried Ledger.
military_doctrine.void_escalation: Offer surveillance that secures the wall and dims the Beacon.

warfront_behavior.negotiation_style: Principled and procedural; insists on accountability and protection guarantees.
warfront_behavior.occupation_style: Protective administration that risks sliding into surveillance and purge.
warfront_behavior.resistance_style: Stubborn warded defense and civic solidarity; brittle where infiltration has rotted trust.

major_locations.economic_function: Hub of warded trade and refuge logistics.
major_locations.magical_function: Anchor of the Beacon network and covenant-oath courts.

major_locations.spiritual_function: Heart of naming-into-the-light and covenant rites.

major_locations.economic_function: Strained intake and forward supply depot.

major_locations.spiritual_function: Confession circles and crowded prayer halls under strain.
major_locations.civilian_function: Last refuge for those fleeing the frontier.
known_secrets: An Ash Ledger cell operates behind a falsified review
major_locations.keeper_attack_vector: Turn the food crisis and infiltration scare into gate closures and purges.

culture.daily_life_summary: Life is ordered by the Beacon's bells and the rhythm of review and refuge; doors are kept lit for strangers, and grievances are meant to be aired in the open.
culture.family_customs: Households swear a guardianship oath for each dependent and keep a refuge-light in the window.
culture.love_and_marriage_customs: Marriages are public covenants witnessed under the Beacon; vows are protective as well as romantic.
culture.education_system: Civic schooling in covenant, due process, and the duty of shelter; clerics teach the rolls and the rites.
culture.work_and_apprenticeship: Guild covenants bind master and apprentice with mutual, reviewable obligations.
culture.food_and_market_life: Warded markets, communal refuge-kitchens, and shared hearth-bread; scarcity strains the old generosity.
culture.funeral_or_death_customs: Naming-into-the-light: the dead are named on the rolls and mourned in the open under the Beacon.
public_honors: A name kept bright on the rolls
taboos: Erasing a name from the rolls
common_sayings: A wall that does not shelter is only a cage.
children_common_beliefs: The Beacon can see a hidden cruelty
A lit window keeps the dark out
Your name on the rolls means you are never truly lost
class_differences: Magistrates and paladins hold the rolls and the oaths; refuge-folk depend on them
Border cities feel forgotten by the bright interior

religion.central_belief: The Beacon shelters all who are named, and protection is holy only when it answers to the protected.
common_prayers_or_oaths: I will shelter and answer for it.
No name lost to the dark.
heresies: The Closed Door (shelter only for the worthy)
sacred_taboos: Turning the ward against the sheltered
religion.relationship_to_death: Death is a return to the light, named and mourned; to die unaccounted in the dark is the true horror.
religion.relationship_to_sacrifice: Sacrifice is the protector's burden borne openly, never demanded of the sheltered.
religion.relationship_to_memory: Memory is the rolls themselves; to be struck from them is to be unmade.
religion.relationship_to_truth: Truth must be aired in review; a buried truth is a broken covenant.
religion.keeper_corruption_strategy: Promote the Pure Light and the Closed Door heresies as truer safety.
religion.void_false_revelation_style: A radiant vision that the watchful, walled city is the only holy one.

internal_power_struggles.title: The Wardenmarch Gates
internal_power_struggles.issue: Whether to close Wardenmarch's gates and impose detention sweeps amid a food crisis and infiltration scare.
internal_power_struggles.public_argument: Inquisitor Vale: 'An open gate in a plague of spies is a death sentence.' Cassia: 'A wall that cages the sheltered is the Abyss's victory, not ours.'
internal_power_struggles.hidden_argument: A collaborator magistrate wants closure to mask an Ash Ledger cell; the Concord fears either choice will break the city.
possible_player_sides: Uphold open shelter and due process with the Covenant
Back containment and detention with the Inquisition
Broker accountable, time-limited screening that keeps the gates open
internal_power_struggles.keeper_best_outcome: The gates close, purges begin, and the Cage of Safety takes hold.
internal_power_struggles.void_best_outcome: Surveillance and registries spread under cover of the crisis.
internal_power_struggles.peaceful_resolution: Transparent, paladin-supervised screening with food relief and no detention without review.

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player uses forbidden soulbinding to save a dying child in Sanctuary territory.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Sanctuary sees life protected through a method that defied accountable order and clean soul-passage.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Brother Calven is grateful but afraid and hides the child; Inquisitor Vale hears partial reports and smells corruption; the Refugee Covenant fears mass suspicion of outsiders.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The child survives, with a soul-scar.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Family gratitude +; soul-flow integrity -2; the act is witnessed in part.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Brother Calven hides the child; the mother is grateful but afraid; Inquisitor Vale opens an investigation.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: A rumor begins, 'the stranger stole a child's soul'; the Purity Inquisition gains political fuel; the Refugee Covenant fears a backlash against vulnerable outsiders.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: The Sanctuary court demands medical records; Brother Calven falsifies documents to protect the child; civic magistrates become involved.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Ash Ledger Covenant weaponizes the scandal — 'Sanctuary condemns the Abyss while hiding illegal soul manipulation' — and Sanctuary's moral authority weakens in diplomacy as Keeper pressure rises.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Interdomain mistrust and a soul-scar that loosens the protected rolls.
cause_effect_examples.void_gain: An Ash Ledger witness has a claim to press later.
player_intervention_options: Confess publicly and submit to ritual review
Find a clean soul-healing method
Expose the Ash Ledger spy
Convince Calven not to falsify records
Ask the child's family to testify truthfully

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player exposes a Sanctuary magistrate secretly collaborating with the Abyss Ash Ledger.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Sanctuary is forced to confront that its order has been hollowed from within.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: The Refugee Covenant and truth-seekers are vindicated; the corrupt magistrate's house falls; the Purity Inquisition exploits the fear to demand sweeping powers.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The collaboration is proven and made public.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Concord legitimacy shaken; the disappeared start being accounted-for; the border Beacon steadies slightly.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Public fear spikes; the Inquisition surges in influence; an Ash Ledger cell scrambles.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Sanctuary trust wobbles — exposure heals the covenant but feeds the paranoia the Keeper wants.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: Either accountable reform or an Inquisition crackdown follows, depending on the player's framing.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: If reform wins, the Beacon brightens and the Keeper loses ground; if paranoia wins, the Cage of Safety advances.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Conditional: large if the exposure fuels purges, small if it fuels accountable reform.
player_intervention_options: Frame the exposure as a call for accountability, not purge
Void the cell's coercive debt contracts
Shield the witnesses from Inquisition reprisal
Back a reformist magistrate over Vale

cause_effect_examples.root_event: Facing a food crisis and infiltration scare, the Concord debates closing Wardenmarch's gates.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Sanctuary's protection collides with its accountability and unity.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: Inquisitor Vale demands closure and sweeps; Cassia and the Covenant demand open shelter and due process; the Concord agonizes.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: Thousands of refugees wait at the gates as the debate drags.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: If closed: refugee morale -10, Covenant trust -; if kept open with screening: Inquisition hostility +, civic anxiety +.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: Closure strands refugees in a corrupted border zone; or open gates strain food to breaking.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Rumors weaponize the choice ('the Concord sold us' or 'the gates let the spies in'); a collaborator exploits the chaos.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: Either a refugee catastrophe or an infiltration incident hardens the city's course.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper gains if protection becomes a cage; it loses ground if accountable screening keeps gates open and trust intact.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Conditional on whether the Cage of Safety takes hold.
player_intervention_options: Broker supervised, time-limited screening
Secure emergency food relief
Expose the collaborator pushing for closure
Rally paladins to guarantee due process at the gates

cause_effect_examples.root_event: An Aegis paladin is ordered by the Inquisition to detain and strike helpless refugee suspects.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Sanctuary's covenant is tested against the demand for obedience.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: The Inquisition insists it is necessary; the Lumen Wardens warn of Beacon harm; the paladin's order is split.
cause_effect_examples.immediate_result: The paladin must choose between the order and the oath.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: If they strike: their oath hollows and the nearest Beacon dims; if they refuse: Inquisition retaliation begins.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: A paladin schism forms; refugees either suffer or are protected; rumors spread either way.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: The covenant either frays toward obedience-magic or reaffirms shelter; recruitment shifts.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: The Aegis orders formally debate whether Inquisition commands can override the oath.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: The Keeper gains if covenant becomes obedience; it loses if the oath of shelter is reaffirmed.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Oath corrosion that dims the Beacons, unless the paladins hold the line.
player_intervention_options: Support the paladin's refusal and shield them
Bring the order to the oath-courts
Expose the detentions to public review
Protect the helpless detainees and restore their names

cause_effect_examples.root_event: The player discovers names being quietly struck from the protected rolls and traces them to soul-debt contracts.
cause_effect_examples.domain_interpretation: Sanctuary recognizes the deepest violation: the sheltered being unmade and harvested.
cause_effect_examples.faction_interpretation: The Lumen Wardens are horrified; the Covenant demands action; the responsible clerk is terrified and coerced.
cause_effect_examples.first_order: Soul-flow integrity -6; the Buried Ledger is partly exposed; the local Beacon flickers.
cause_effect_examples.second_order: The coerced clerk may confess or flee; the Ash Ledger presses its claims; fear rises.
cause_effect_examples.third_order: Restoring names re-lights the ward, but the scandal feeds the Inquisition's case for control.
cause_effect_examples.fourth_order: A reckoning over the archives forces either real accountability or a cover-up.
cause_effect_examples.fifth_order: If names are restored and contracts voided, the Beacon brightens and the Keeper is denied; if buried, the disappearance spreads.
cause_effect_examples.keeper_gain: Conditional on whether the disappeared are restored to the light.
player_intervention_options: Restore the disappeared to the rolls
Void the coercive soul-debt contracts
Protect and turn the coerced clerk
Bring the archive reckoning to public review under the Beacon

metaphysical: Can a name fully harvested into soul-debt be restored to the rolls and the light, or only mourned?
Does a Beacon dim from a single broken oath, or only from a pattern of betrayal?
political: Can accountable governance survive a genuine infiltration crisis without becoming the Inquisition?
How captured are the review-courts by the Buried Ledger?
magic: Is there any ethical bounded surveillance-ward, or does every inward ward begin the Cage of Safety?
Can a hollowed paladin oath be re-sworn whole?
faction: Is the Purity Inquisition reformable, or is it already the Keeper's instrument?
How deep does Ash Ledger infiltration run in the Concord?
npc: Can Inquisitor Vale be turned from paranoia, or only stopped?
Will Brother Calven's protective lies save the child or doom them both?
war_economy: How long can the refuges feed a swelling population before gate closures become inevitable?
What happens to civic trust if a major Beacon goes dark?
implementation: Should the protected rolls be modeled as a registry entity linked to soul-flow wounds and Ash Ledger debt?
Should 'gate closure' be a location/policy state with cascading domain effects?

locked_decisions: Sanctuary magic and authority must always rest on accountable covenant; protection without accountability is its corruption.
Sanctuary corruption must distort protection into control (the Cage of Safety) and unity into purity-paranoia, never become generic darkness.
Sanctuary internal politics must respect the Concord / Inquisition / Covenant / paladin fracture.
Erasing a name from the protected rolls or disappearing the sheltered is the violation Sanctuary cannot forgive.
Beacon wards and covenant magic weaken when oaths are broken in secret or the sheltered are betrayed.
Mercy is honored in Sanctuary only when it is paired with accountability.
